== Problem ==

Antonette gets <math> 70 \% </math> on a 10-problem test, <math> 80 \% </math> on a 20-problem test and <math> 90 \% </math> on a 30-problem test. If the three tests are combined into one 60-problem test, which percent is closest to her overall score? 

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 40\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 77\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 80\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 83\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 87 </math>

== Solution ==

<math> 70 \% \cdot 10=7 </math>

<math> 80 \% \cdot 20=16 </math>

<math> 90 \% \cdot 30=27 </math>

Adding them up gets <math> 7+16+27=50 </math>. The overall percentage correct would be <math> \frac{50}{60}=\frac{5}{6}=5 \cdot 16.\overline{6}=83.\overline{3} \approx \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 83} </math>.
